thread:
anya: Hey team, customer WispPay just opened a high-sev ticket (INC-20987). They see intermittent 502/504s and long tail latencies when doing back-to-back embed+generate calls. Affects ~30% of requests during peak. Repro attached.

sam: Got the ticket, assigning to oncall. Any quick context from logs?

maria: I pulled the gateway logs for their org_id=org_wisp. Patterns: auth refresh errors spike then a flood of backend connection resets. snippet: `2026-03-14T18:07:12Z auth: token_refresh_fail user=svc-wisp err=429` then within ~2s we see `upstream_error: connection_reset` and 502s.

kevin: Important detail: customer uses our JS SDK v0.9.2 with automatic token refresh (their token is rotated every 5m by their infra). SDK does naive parallel refresh — multiple inflight requests trigger simultaneous refreshes. That causes auth backend fanout and transient 429s.

anya: Interesting. So token 429 -> gateway closes connections -> requests retry and pile up -> we return 5xx?

maria: Yep. Also noticed elevated token validation latency at the auth service: `auth.latency_p95` jumped from 30ms -> 800ms during the fanout. Gateway retries amplify the load.

sam: Do we have a repro script? Can we reproduce in staging to confirm mitigation?

kevin: I wrote a small repro. JS snippet: 
```
const Redwood = require('@redwood/sdk');
const client = new Redwood.Client({token: process.env.TOKEN, autoRefresh: true});
for (let i=0;i<200;i++) {
  client.embed({input: 'test '+i});
  client.generate({prompt: 'short '+i});
}
```
Run with a short-lived token that expires every 10s and you'll see the cascade.

maria: Reproduced in our staging with TOKEN_TTL=10s. Observed same token_refresh_fail -> gateway_conn_reset -> 502.

anya: Short-term mitigation for WispPay?

sam: Support workaround: ask them to pin token refresh to single-thread (serialise refresh), or upgrade SDK to v0.10.0-beta which has in-flight refresh dedupe. Also suggest increasing client-side backoff/retry jitter.

kevin: On our side, I can deploy a gateway config that tolerates transient auth 429s by returning 401 to client rather than immediately resetting connection, giving SDK a chance to refresh before connection drops. That should reduce the number of 5xx seen by the customer.

maria: We should also throttle auth validation fanout: put a short-lived LRU cache for token lookups on auth nodes and a leaky bucket limiter per org. Will prepare a patch.

anya: What are asks for product/pm?

sam: Need comms template for WispPay: explain root cause (token-refresh fanout), temporary mitigation steps, ETA for SDK patch and gateway change. Also flag billing — customer reported unexpected token-refresh counts causing billing spike. Need billing to check whether to credit.

kevin: Billing note: when SDK refreshes in parallel, it incs token validation count and also triggers extra metering for auth calls we bill. Ticket Billing-4321 opened to assess credits.

maria: Plan: (1) immediate support email to WispPay with workaround (pin/serialize refresh + upgrade SDK beta) — <30m, (2) gateway config change to reduce churn — rollout in next 2 hours as a canary, (3) auth service cache+throttle patch targeted EOD, (4) SDK release v0.10.0 with dedupe in 24-48h.

anya: I'll draft the customer message. @kevin can you prod the canary deploy? @maria please attach the staging repro logs to the ticket.

kevin: deploy-bot: starting canary for gateway-tolerant-auth at revision r245.

deploy-bot: canary started: 3% traffic -> gateway-tolerant-auth r245 (canary-id c-5589).

maria: Canary looks OK on our staging probe for the next 10m: auth 429s still happen but we now return 401 to client and keep upstream connections healthy. Customer synthetic tests show a drop in 502s from 32% -> 4%.

sam: Great. I'll update WispPay with the canary result and the temporary billing hold. Draft: "We identified a token-refresh fanout between your short-lived tokens and the SDK, causing a cascade of retries and gateway resets. We've deployed a canary that reduces 502s for you. Please try upgrading the SDK or serializing refresh as a fix. We're also reviewing billing impact." Thoughts?

anya: LGTM. Add steps to reproduce and the repro script. Also ask them to send traces with org headers if they still see 5xx.

kevin: I'll prepare the SDK beta release and docs for `autoRefresh` dedupe. Also adding a runtime flag `redwood.refresh.serial=true` for a quick toggle.

maria: I'll open PR for auth LRU cache + per-org leaky bucket (PR #1482).

sam: Action items tracked: INC-20987 (customer comms, support), DEPLOY-8492 (gateway canary), AUTH-1482 (cache+throttle), SDK-110 (dedupe release), BILL-4321 (billing review).

anya: Sending customer msg now.

anya: @wisppay-ops Hi — quick update: we've deployed a canary that should reduce the 502/504s you saw. Short-term workaround: upgrade to SDK v0.10.0-beta or set refresh to serial. We're investigating billing impact, will follow up within 24h. — Anya (support) :wave:

support-bot: message sent to customer channel #wisppay-support (inc:INC-20987).

kevin: Can we add a monitoring alert to catch token_refresh_fanout for other orgs? Recommend a new alert: `auth.refresh.parallel_spike > 50/min for org -> page oncall`.

maria: Added alert prototype to ops board, linking to runbook.

sam: Thanks all. Keep this thread updated with deploy progress and customer replies.

anya: Customer replied: "we see immediate improvement, thanks. We'll test more and report." Closing loop once billing decision done.

maria: Will follow up when PR merges.

kevin: SDK beta published to npm: @redwood/sdk@0.10.0-beta. Docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/refresh-dedupe.

deploy-bot: canary c-5589 promoted to 25% after successful health checks.

deploy-bot: canary promoted to stable at 02:10 UTC.

sam: Closing for now. Reopen if we see reoccurrence. Thanks team :tada:
